 A comment from an ex-employee on HN explains the broader situation. For those who are interested in digging further.

 tl;dr: It's scaling. Nothing special about GH. There's a data centre and systems migration happening while the their traffic is exploding due to LLMs speeding the dev cycle putting under pressure every known and unknown bottleneck in their system, which happens to anybody who scales at that pace and volume.

 What the person in the comment says makes a lot of sense to some degree, but I do feel it brushes aside the fact that GitHub has been going downhill (in terms of availability) for years now. So if anything, opening the AI flood gates made things even worse rather than being the root cause on its own.

 The tone of the comment also comes across as "Be grateful you peasants, how dare you complain?" (for a lack of better phrasing), which doesn't really help their case. For example:

 Did you notice that over 50% of GitHub read traffic is now being served from Azure instead of GitHub's own data centers, and growing, and that all GitHub Monolith traffic is scheduled to be served from Azure instead of GitHub's data centers by the end of CY26?

 GitLab ran on Azure for a while because we got a bunch of free credits through Hacker News. That was supposed to be enough for a year or so, but we burned through them in just a few months. We ran away screaming from Azure because it was a flaming pile of shit. So maybe boasting about moving to Azure is not such a great thing to do.
